meta.title: Bumimic — an open recorder for listening to nature
meta.description: A pocket-sized acoustic recorder that listens above human hearing, logs the weather, and keeps going for months on three AA cells.

hero.title: Hear what
hero.lede: A pocket-sized recorder that listens above the range of human hearing, logs the weather around it, and keeps going for months on three AA cells.
hero.tagline: Assembled and tested. Open hardware. Ships from Zurich.

board.imageAlt: Render of the Bumimic prototype circuit board, showing the microSD slot, radio module and sensors
board.caption: Board render — board-v0.3, top-down on white

ultrasonic.title: Listens up to 192 kHz
ultrasonic.body: Ultrasonic audio is written straight to a microSD card, on a schedule you set or whenever a trigger fires. The recordings never leave your hands.

sensors.title: Reads the weather around it
sensors.body: Temperature, humidity, light, pressure and movement are logged beside the audio, so a sighting arrives with the conditions that produced it.

alerts.title: Tells you when something happens
alerts.body: Event alerts travel over LoRaWAN to whoever is watching the site. Only the alert travels — the audio stays on the card until you collect it.

battery.title: Leave it out there
battery.body: A few microamps at rest and three AA cells to draw from. Deployments are measured in months, and any shop that sells batteries can keep one running.

specs.boardCaption: Board detail — mic, sensors, microSD, radio

0.title: Ultrasonic microphone
0.body: Tuned for bats and insects, not speech.

2.title: LoRaWAN radio
2.body: Regional settings for Kenya, Brazil, Philippines.

3.title: microSD storage
3.body: Up to 512 GB of recordings on a single card.

order.title: Configure your order
order.subtitle: Every choice for the order sits here — the regional radio build, a case if you want one, and where it ships.

region.label: Regional build
region.note: Radio settings are fixed at build time, so pick the country the device will live in.

addons.label: Add-ons — pick any, or none
addons.note: The waterproof case is sealed for wet-season deployment; the printed case is lighter and its files are open, so you can print your own. Accessory prices are provisional.

specifications.title: Specifications
specifications.subtitle: The numbers, for the people who need them. Everything here is from the current prototype and may change before the first production run.

audio.title: Audio
audio.content: Ultrasonic capture to 192 kHz sample rate, 16-bit, written to microSD. Continuous, scheduled or trigger-based recording.

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.content: Temperature, humidity, light, pressure and movement. Every detection arrives with the conditions that produced it.

power.title: Power
power.content: Three AA or AAA cells with USB-C for setup. A few microamps at rest means deployments measured in months.

radio.title: Radio and regional builds
radio.content: LoRaWAN radio tuned for each region: Kenya (EU868), Brazil (AU915), Philippines (AS923). Radio settings are fixed at build time.

size.title: Size and enclosure
size.content: 57 × 47 mm board, four-layer — slightly smaller than an AudioMoth in both directions. Optional waterproof or 3D-printed case.

open.title: Open hardware
open.content: Schematic, board layout, manufacturing files and firmware are all developed in public. Build, repair and adapt it yourself.
